transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

That pattern most often points to an intermittent door-latch/interlock switch or door alignment issue.

If the microwave goes quiet / stops heating but the display remains on, then opening and firmly closing the door makes it resume, one of the door switches may be momentarily losing contact. The switches are safety devices, so the oven treats it as though the door has opened.

Less commonly it could be a control-board relay or an overheating issue, but an overheat cut-out normally needs time to cool before it resets; it would not usually recover immediately just from operating the door.

Things you can safely check:

• Clean the door latch hooks and the receiver slots in the front frame. Grease or food debris can prevent full engagement. Use a dry cloth or lightly dampened cloth only; do not spray cleaner into the latch area.
• Check the door closes firmly, is not sagging, and has no obvious play, damaged hooks, bent hinges, or damaged seal area.
• Note what happens when it faults:
• Does the internal light, fan and turntable stop as well?
• Does the countdown pause, or continue counting down?
• Does it make any unusual buzzing, clicking, smell hot, or spark?
• Test only with a cup of water inside — never run it empty — and stay with it.

Do not remove the casing or attempt to adjust/bypass the door switches. Microwaves contain hazardous high-voltage components even after unplugging, and the interlock system is safety-critical.

As it is intermittent but recurring, I would arrange a Bosch-approved appliance engineer, particularly if it is in warranty. Give them the model BFL524MS0B and the FD/E-Nr from the rating plate, and describe that “cooking intermittently stops and resumes after opening/closing the door.” That should direct them to check the latch/interlock switches, mounts, wiring and control board.

Stop using it pending repair if the door is loose or damaged, there is arcing/burning smell, or — especially — it ever appears to run with the door open.

When it stops, the fan and light cut out as if the door was opened. The time stays on the display and the start indicator goes off. There's no smell, sparks or buzzing. I cleaned some grease off the door hooks and latch slots, but it has still happened once since. The door might sit very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be sure. It's out of warranty, but I'd pay for a Bosch engineer.

Those extra details make an intermittent door-interlock/latch issue very likely.

The key clues are:

• Fan and light stop exactly as if the door has been opened.
• The cooking time remains displayed rather than the oven fully losing power.
• The start indicator goes out.
• Opening and closing the door restores operation.
• Possible slight droop on the handle side.

The control is therefore probably receiving an intermittent “door open” signal. Likely causes, in order, are:

1. A worn or intermittent door interlock microswitch
2. A loose/cracked interlock-switch mounting bracket or latch receiver
3. Slight door/hinge sag meaning the hooks do not reliably hold the switches operated
4. Less likely, wiring or the control board input for the interlock circuit

This does not sound like a magnetron, inverter, or cooling problem.

Cleaning the hooks and slots was sensible, but since it has recurred, it needs a proper inspection. Do not try to bend the hooks, pack out the latch, adjust switches, or remove the built-in unit/casing yourself. The safety switches are deliberately designed so that incorrect adjustment can create a hazardous condition.

A Bosch engineer is a reasonable choice, especially for an integrated model. When booking, describe it specifically as:

> “The microwave intermittently stops mid-cycle. Light and fan cut out, the timer remains on the display but the Start indicator goes off, as though the door has opened. Opening and closing the door allows operation again. Possible slight door sag on the handle side.”

Ask them to inspect the complete door interlock system: door hooks, hinges, latch/switch carrier, microswitches, wiring and control-board connection.

Have the E-Nr and FD numbers from the rating plate ready; Bosch use those to identify the exact production version and parts. On a built-in microwave the rating label is often visible around the door opening or side frame when the door is open.

Until it is repaired, I would avoid leaving it running unattended. It is probably failing safe — stopping rather than continuing to heat — but it may become more frequent or eventually refuse to start. Stop using it altogether if the door becomes noticeably loose, it starts operating unpredictably, or it ever runs when the door is not properly closed.
